title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook: Process, Runbooks, Rotations, Game Days, and Comms Templates
author: Avery Chen
content:
Summary
-------
This playbook describes Redwood Inference’s on-call and incident response program. It covers the end-to-end incident lifecycle, runbook templates, on-call rotations, game day guidance, postmortem requirements, and customer & status-page communications templates. The goal is fast detection, safe mitigation, and clear post-incident learning.

Scope and audience
------------------
- Scope: All production-facing services (hosted API, Dedicated control plane, Private control plane) and their supporting infra (GPU fleet, routing, auth, billing).
- Audience: on-call engineers, SREs, service owners, incident commanders (ICs), customer success for external comms, and managers tracking reliability metrics.

Incident lifecycle (4 phases)
----------------------------
1. Detection & Triage
   - Alerts via PagerDuty/Snowflake integrations, automated anomaly detectors, or customer-reported tickets.
   - Triage goal: confirm alert validity within 5 minutes for P0/P1, 30 minutes for P2.
2. Mitigation & Stabilization
   - Assign roles (IC, scribe, communications lead, subject-matter experts).
   - Apply runbook steps to restore service or apply a safe mitigation/fallback.
   - Target: restore customer-visible functionality or apply graceful degradation within SLO-agreed windows (see SLO table below).
3. Recovery & Validate
   - Monitor for recurrence for a minimum of 60 minutes after mitigation.
   - Run synthetic checks and customer-facing scenario tests.
4. Post-incident Learning
   - Postmortem created within 72 hours (initial draft) and finalized within 14 days.

Priority definitions & SLO thresholds
------------------------------------
| Priority | Impact example | PagerDuty level | Target response | Target mitigation window |
|----------|----------------|-----------------|-----------------|--------------------------|
| P0 (SEV0) | Complete outage (API 100% unavailable for a region) | PagerDuty: page all on-call | 5 minutes | 15 min to global mitigation or circuit breaker |
| P1 (SEV1) | Severe degradation (latency > 10x, errors > 20%) | Page IC + primary on-call | 5 minutes | 60 minutes to mitigation |
| P2 (SEV2) | Partial feature degradation or single-customer impact | Page primary on-call | 30 minutes | 4 hours to mitigation |
| P3 | Non-urgent/investigation | Email/ticket | 24 hours | 3 business days to triage |

Roles and responsibilities
--------------------------
- Incident Commander (IC): owns coordination and declaration of incident priority.
- Scribe: documents timeline, actions, and communications in the incident channel and status page.
- SME responders: engineers with deep knowledge of the affected service(s).
- Communications lead: owns status updates to customers and internal stakeholders.
- Postmortem owner: drives RCA, corrective actions, and tracking to completion.

Escalation matrix (summary)
--------------------------
1. PagerDuty primary -> 2. Secondary -> 3. Team on-call lead -> 4. EngSRE manager -> 5. CTO on-call (for > 2-hour unresolved P0).

On-call rotations and expectations
--------------------------------
- Rotation model: two-week primary rotation per team with a separate pager for secondary/backup. Most teams mirror a primary/secondary split.
- Handoff: each shift must document handoff summary in the team on-call doc and in Slack (channel #oncall-handovers) including active incidents, ongoing mitigations, and pager silences.
- Weekly commitments: primary handles pages and triage; secondary supports escalations and complex mitigations.
- Out-of-hours: primary must acknowledge within defined targets; if unreachable after escalation policy, proceed to secondary.
- Time-off: engineers must post future out-of-office dates to the rotation calendar two weeks in advance and swap shifts using the rota tool.

Runbook style guide
-------------------
- Runbooks are actionable, single-source-of-truth documents for common incidents. Each runbook MUST include:
  - Symptoms & detection signals (metrics, logs, alerts)
  - Quick mitigation steps (3–6 steps for immediate action)
  - Full recovery procedure (detailed safe rollback / restart steps)
  - Post-incident validation checks
  - Owner and last test date
- Keep runbook steps idempotent and include exact CLI commands and dashboard links.

Example runbook: API 5xx spike (service: inference-api)
-----------------------------------------------------
Summary: sudden increase in 5xx from the inference API.
Detection signals:
- error_rate(inference-api, 5xx) > 5% for 5m
- upstream latency > 500ms p95

Quick mitigation (execute in order):
1. Page team + declare SEV1 if customer impact observed.
2. Switch traffic to fallback model variant via routing console:
   - CLI: redwoodctl routing set-weight --service inference-api --variant model-7b-q4f32 --weight 0.8
3. Temporarily increase autoscaler min_replicas to absorb backlog:
   - kubectl patch hpa inference-api -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":8}}'
4. If memory OOMs present, set environment variable to reduce batch size and restart pods:
   - kubectl rollout restart deployment/inference-api

Full recovery steps:
- Collect logs with timeframe: 2026-02-10T10:00Z to 2026-02-10T10:30Z
- Revert routing after stability observed for 30 minutes: redwoodctl routing revert --service inference-api --to-saved stable-2026-02-10
- Validate with synthetic requests and customer-critical flows.

Post-incident validation checklist:
- p95 latency < 200ms for 30m
- 5xx < 0.5% for 30m
- No customer complaints opened in last 60m

Postmortem template & timeline
------------------------------
Required timeline:
1. Incident declared: IC assigns postmortem owner.
2. Within 72 hours: initial postmortem draft with timeline and mitigation steps.
3. Within 7 calendar days: complete RCA and action items with owners.
4. Within 14 days: final postmortem published and linked on status page if customer-visible.

Postmortem content (minimum fields):
- Title (short): e.g., "2026-02-10: inference-api 5xx spike (SEV1)"
- Incident lead / owner
- Start / end times (UTC)
- Severity level
- Impact summary (customers, regions, data exposure if any)
- Timeline (ordered events, timestamps)
- Root cause analysis (why the root problem existed)
- Contributing factors (process, monitoring gaps, etc.)
- Corrective actions (owner and due date)
- Preventative actions & follow-ups
- Metrics dashboard links and log slices

Game days and readiness exercises
--------------------------------
Purpose: validate runbooks, on-call processes, and cross-team coordination.
Frequency: quarterly team game days and annual cross-org large-scale exercise.
Game day format:
1. Planning (1 week prior): define blast radius, objectives, injects, and observers.
2. Execution (2–4 hours): run simulated incident, require real on-call to respond using live runbooks.
3. Debrief (1–2 hours): collect feedback, update runbooks, and publish a short runbook-change log.
Success metrics:
- Mean time to acknowledge < 5m for primary pages during exercise.
- Mean time to mitigation < 30m for P1 scenarios.
- Runbook completeness score (post-game checklist) >= 80%.

Status page and customer communications templates
------------------------------------------------
Status page categories
- Operational, Degraded, Partial Outage, Major Outage.
- Each page entry must include: start time, expected ETA (if known), summary, affected regions, mitigation steps in progress, and next update time.

Internal status update cadence (IC owns):
- Initial internal update within 15 minutes for P0/P1.
- External status (public status page) within 30 minutes of declaration for customer-visible incidents.
- Updates every 30 minutes until recovery, then 60 minutes while validating.

Public status page template (example text)
- Title: "Partial outage: inference API in us-west-2"
- Start time: 2026-02-10T10:03Z
- Summary: We are investigating an elevated error rate affecting text generation requests in us-west-2. We have routed traffic to fallback variants and are monitoring.
- Impact: Intermittent 5xx errors and increased latency for a subset of customers in us-west-2.
- Next update: 2026-02-10T10:33Z

Customer comms email template (short)
Subject: Redwood Incident: impact to inference API (us-west-2)
Body:
Hello {CustomerName},

We experienced elevated errors and latency for inference requests in us-west-2 starting at 2026-02-10T10:03Z. Our engineering team applied a traffic routing mitigation and is continuing validation. We will update you by 2026-02-10T10:33Z or earlier.

If you have questions or critical dependencies, reply to this email and mark urgent.

— Redwood Inference Support

Slack + PagerDuty templates
- Incident channel name: #inc-<short-id>-<service> (example: #inc-20260210-inference-api).
- Initial Slack message (by IC):
  "SEV1 declared — inference-api (us-west-2). IC: @avery. Scribe: @marcus. Impact: 5xx spike affecting generation. PagerDuty triggered. Status page: <link>."

Operational tools & CLI snippets
------------------------------
- PagerDuty: escalate: pd escalation-rule run --service inference-api --policy severity-escalation
- Patch manifests: kubectl patch ... (see runbook examples)
- Status page API (example):
  curl -X POST "https://status.redwood.ai/api/v1/incidents" -H "Authorization: Bearer ${STATUS_API_TOKEN}" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"title":"Partial outage: inference-api","status":"investigating","impact":"intermittent 5xx in us-west-2","started_at":"2026-02-10T10:03Z"}'

Ownership & tracking
--------------------
- Postmortem action items are tracked in the reliability board (JIRA project: REL). Every action must have an owner and due date and be linked back into the postmortem page.
- Quarterly reliability review: each team presents significant incidents (> P1) and status of outstanding corrective actions.

Appendix A — Contact matrix (example)
| Role | Primary | Secondary | Pager | Slack |
|------|---------|-----------|-------|-------|
| Inference API owner | @inference-owner | @inference-backup | inference-api-pager | #sv-inference |
| GPU Fleet | @gpu-sre | @gpu-backup | gpu-fleet-pager | #sv-gpu |

Appendix B — Runbook maintenance checklist
- Review runbooks after each SEV1/SEV0 incident.
- Full runbook audit every 6 months.

Appendix C — Example postmortem excerpt
- Summary: "We mis-routed traffic to an untested variant after autoscaler flapping caused a pod churn. Root cause: autoscaler configuration allowed spike-based scale-down to zero. Fix: change autoscaler cooldown and add pre-deploy validation for routing weights."
